_title: Electrical Stimulation (ES) and Electromagnetic Therapy for the Treatment of Wounds

criteria.text: Covered only for one of the four listed chronic ulcer types
sub_conditions: chronic Stage III or Stage IV pressure ulcers
criteria.source_span: will only be covered for chronic Stage III or Stage IV pressure ulcers, arterial ulcers, diabetic ulcers, and venous stasis ulcers.

criteria.text: Chronic ulcers are defined as ulcers that have not healed within 30 days of occurrence
criteria.source_span: Chronic ulcers are defined as ulcers that have not healed within 30 days of occurrence.

criteria.text: Covered only after appropriate standard wound therapy has been tried for at least 30 days with no measurable signs of improved healing
criteria.source_span: ES or electromagnetic therapy will be covered only after appropriate standard wound therapy has been tried for at least 30 days and there are no measurable signs of improved healing.

criteria.text: Measurable signs of improved healing include decrease in wound size, exudates, and necrotic tissue
sub_conditions: a decrease in wound size (either surface area or volume)
decrease in amount of necrotic tissue
criteria.source_span: Measurable signs of improved healing include: a decrease in wound size (either surface area or volume), decrease in amount of exudates, and decrease in amount of necrotic tissue.

criteria.text: Standard wound care includes nutritional optimization, debridement, moist granulation bed maintenance, and infection treatment
sub_conditions: debridement by any means to remove devitalized tissue
maintenance of a clean, moist bed of granulation tissue with appropriate moist dressings
necessary treatment to resolve any infection that may be present
criteria.source_span: Standard wound care includes: optimization of nutritional status, debridement by any means to remove devitalized tissue, maintenance of a clean, moist bed of granulation tissue with appropriate moist dressings, and necessary treatment to resolve any infection that may be present.

criteria.text: Therapy must be discontinued when the wound demonstrates 100% epithelialized wound bed
criteria.source_span: ES or electromagnetic therapy must be discontinued when the wound demonstrates 100% epitheliliazed wound bed.

criteria.text: Services can only be covered when performed by a physician, physical therapist, or incident to a physician service
criteria.source_span: ES and electromagnetic therapy services can only be covered when performed by a physician, physical therapist, or incident to a physician service.

criteria.text: If used, wounds must be evaluated at least monthly by the treating physician
criteria.source_span: If ES or electromagnetic therapy is being used, wounds must be evaluated at least monthly by the treating physician.

criteria.text: The practitioner must evaluate the wound and contact the treating physician if the wound worsens
criteria.source_span: the practitioner must evaluate the wound and contact the treating physician if the wound worsens.

criteria.text: Will not be covered as an initial treatment modality
criteria.source_span: ES and electromagnetic therapy will not be covered as an initial treatment modality.

criteria.text: Continued treatment is not covered if measurable signs of healing are not demonstrated within any 30-day treatment period
criteria.source_span: Continued treatment with ES or electromagnetic therapy is not covered if measurable signs of healing have not been demonstrated within any 30-day period of treatment.

criteria.text: Unsupervised use will not be covered as not medically reasonable and necessary
criteria.source_span: Unsupervised use of ES or electromagnetic therapy for wound therapy will not be covered, as this use has not been found to be medically reasonable and necessary.

criteria.text: Medicare allows either one covered ES therapy or one covered electromagnetic therapy for wound treatment, not both
criteria.source_span: This means Medicare will allow either one covered ES therapy or one covered electromagnetic therapy for the treatment of wounds.

notes: q4 quotes the source's own typo ('epitheliliazed') verbatim for exact grounding.
